Editionskompass

An invitation to scholarly editors.

Interested in Git and what it could offer your editorial work? We start with your questions.

Bring technology and editorial responsibility together

Git is often left to a project’s technical partners. Yet it can preserve decisions, document their development and shape collaboration. Choosing suitable working practices and deciding which traces to preserve, share or analyse requires editorial judgement. Technical advice and editorial responsibility belong together.

Four project types for orientation

From an individual project and a long-term edition to a public corpus and a typical grant-funded project: no two undertakings are alike. Fictional examples make common decisions tangible, helping you recognise your situation and prepare an appropriate Git strategy, including for a proposal or workshop.

Others will read our repositories.

Published edition data are not the only interesting reading. Working repositories can be fascinating sources, preserving traces of decisions, collaboration, detours and changes.

There are legitimate reasons to read these sources with editorial care: joining a team, reviewing a project or researching editorial practice. Such readings may reveal connections we did not notice while working. AI-assisted analysis can also open up unexpected perspectives.

We present four selected perspectives. If you are planning to use Git, consider these viewpoints: what should others be able to understand? What may they read and analyse? And which conclusions do the recorded traces actually support?

Explore, try, take away

Stories introduce a topic; takeaways, practical recommendations and templates help you act. Myth/fact and antipattern questions offer optional short challenges. Nobody needs to answer every question. All 108 topics are also collected for reading and download.
